seoTitle: Perfume Bottle and Travel Spray Box Fit | MTT

Record maximum body and cap dimensions, filled weights and label boundaries for each. sections: Start with the filled components

A capped full-size bottle and a slim travel spray can look like a matched pair while behaving very differently in an insert. Record maximum body and cap dimensions, filled weights and label boundaries for each. Mark where the product may touch the support and where it must not: a decorated cap, sprayed label or loose collar may be unsuitable as the primary grip. Supply representative physical components before freezing the cavity drawing.
Separate location from lifting

A cavity that keeps the bottle centred does not necessarily let the customer lift it safely. Show the finger entry and withdrawal direction in the section drawing. For a tall bottle, assess the path of the cap and shoulder as it pivots out; for a narrow vial, test whether the grip can reach the body without pulling the cap. A small finger notch changes the available contact area, so review retention again after adding it.
Check the book lid and hinge as a system

Close the lid over the complete loaded insert, including card and tissue if specified. The tallest item, hinge fold and any closure components all consume space. First locate a witness mark or interference point; change the support height or envelope only after identifying what touches. A flush empty shell is not evidence that a loaded sample will close reliably.
Illustrative sample decision

A brand changes the travel spray to a larger cap after artwork approval. Do not enlarge both cavities immediately. Compare the replacement cap against the original cavity, the bottle extraction path and the lid underside. Record the sample revision, try removal with the full-size bottle still present, and submit the altered pack for the agreed distribution review if the change could affect performance. ISTA explains why changes in product size, packaging or distribution may call for retesting: ISTA retesting guidance.
Request comparable quotations

Provide both components, filled weights, quantity per design, destination, print files, preferred closure and required launch date. Request separate lines for shell, insert, decoration, sampling, tooling and freight. MTT can review a custom sample brief; minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, sample charges and other fees.
Compare two packing sequences

In one sequence the full-size bottle is inserted first, followed by the travel spray and then the card. In another the card sits beneath the pair. These are different specifications: the card must not bow over the bottle, snag the closure or cover the removal notch. Mark the card position and print face on the assembly instruction. Have a person unfamiliar with the concept pack and unpack the complete sample and note any point requiring force.
Compare support materials honestly

Folded paperboard can provide a printable platform and geometry through folds; a shaped insert made from another material may better accommodate a particular contour. Neither name proves drop performance or surface compatibility. Ask the supplier to identify the proposed substrate, accessible area, contact surfaces and sample cost. Compare two options with the same filled bottles and the same outer pack rather than ranking them on appearance alone.

title: Two Candle Jars in a Drawer Gift Box: Fit, Weight and Separation
seoTitle: Two Candle Jars in a Drawer Gift Box | MTT
summary: Begin with the filled, capped jars, not a nominal capacity. Compare the largest body, lid and label envelope for every scent, and weigh each finished component. Record whether lid edges, decorated glass.
intro: Begin with the filled, capped jars, not a nominal capacity. Compare the largest body, lid and label envelope for every scent, and weigh each finished component. Record whether lid edges, decorated glass or labels may contact an insert. A heavier variant can alter the drawer load even when the outside diameter is unchanged.
cta: Share your filled product dimensions, weight, quantity per design and destination. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 in product value per order; freight, samples and other fees are excluded.
sections: Measure the actual candle set

Begin with the filled, capped jars, not a nominal capacity. Compare the largest body, lid and label envelope for every scent, and weigh each finished component. Record whether lid edges, decorated glass or labels may contact an insert. A heavier variant can alter the drawer load even when the outside diameter is unchanged.
Locate both jars and protect the gap

Lay out the pair in the actual packing orientation. Check the wall between cavities as well as clearance at the outer tray edges. The material must retain the jars during the intended handling while leaving enough access to remove either one independently. A tray with impressive top presentation may conceal insufficient base support, so review a section drawing and the assembled sample together.
Inspect the loaded drawer travel

With both jars and the accessory in place, open and close the drawer throughout its travel. Check if the tray sags, catches the sleeve or shifts as the loaded end passes the sleeve edge. Inspect the pull attachment and the base of the tray; do not infer a load rating from ribbon appearance. Establish who carries out any agreed load or transit test and record acceptance conditions before sampling.
Illustrative size variation

If a seasonal candle uses a taller lid but the same glass jar, place that complete variant in the approved tray. Compare the highest point with the sleeve interior and observe the label and lid during repeated opening. If contact appears, decide whether to alter support height, sleeve clearance or the set layout, then document the revision and repeat the relevant review.
Give the supplier a complete scope

Send jar dimensions and filled weight for each scent, intended carrying and shipping route, quantities by artwork, and a note on label-sensitive areas. Ask for shell, insert, optional tool, sample, tooling and freight to be quoted separately. A presentation drawer is not, by itself, a validated shipping pack. See ISTA test selection guidance: ISTA test selection guidance. Orders start at 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order; freight, samples and other fees are excluded.
Compare the insert approaches

A folded board cradle can separate two regular shapes with walls and locating folds. A shaped insert may reproduce more of a jar profile. Both need review where the base carries weight, at the rim and around the label. Ask for the same jar orientation, finger access and available height when comparing samples; material alone does not establish protection.
Plan the retail and shipping handoff

A retailer may carry the drawer by its sleeve; a warehouse may pack it flat in a larger shipping carton. Tell the supplier which orientation and handling are expected, and do not assume the presentation sleeve is the transport closure. Agree the actual outer pack, any protective wrap and the acceptance conditions with the logistics team. A generic sample drop cannot establish performance for every route.

title: A Candle Gift Box With a Wick Tool: Plan the Accessory Channel
seoTitle: Candle Gift Box Wick Tool Insert Guide | MTT
summary: Measure the complete tool in its packed condition, including loops, hinges, sleeves or a protective cover. Note any surface that can scratch glass, ink or foil. Confirm which party supplies and packs the.
intro: Measure the complete tool in its packed condition, including loops, hinges, sleeves or a protective cover. Note any surface that can scratch glass, ink or foil. Confirm which party supplies and packs the tool. A rendered accessory illustrates a possible layout; the customer’s actual object controls the recess.
cta: Share your filled product dimensions, weight, quantity per design and destination. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 in product value per order; freight, samples and other fees are excluded.
sections: Define the accessory, including sharp and moving parts

Measure the complete tool in its packed condition, including loops, hinges, sleeves or a protective cover. Note any surface that can scratch glass, ink or foil. Confirm which party supplies and packs the tool. A rendered accessory illustrates a possible layout; the customer’s actual object controls the recess.
Choose a removal sequence before die-cutting

If the customer must remove the tool before the candle, make its grip visible and accessible without levering against the jar. Compare a dedicated paperboard pocket, strap or separate wrapped compartment using the actual part. The chosen retention must allow removal without trapping a finger or dropping the accessory into the presentation box.
Keep hard edges apart

Place a physical boundary between a metal component and glass or labelled surfaces. Check both the position at rest and the positions it can reach if the assembled box is turned. If a protective sleeve is proposed, include it in the cavity dimensions and the packing instructions; a loose sleeve may migrate during handling.
Record the sample, not a universal tolerance

Mark the actual tool revision, tray material, folds, adhesive areas and sample version. Inspect the contact points after the supplier and buyer agree representative handling conditions. A simple observation on one sample is not a certified transport result. Review the full distribution pack and whether a changed tool, material or route requires new testing: ISTA retesting guidance.
Ask for a useful quote

Supply the tool drawing and physical sample, filled candle dimensions and weight, approved artwork, quantities and destination. Ask for accessory packing, any protective sleeve, insert and shell as distinct scope items. MTT can assess the packaging brief; projects start at 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, sample and other fees.
Compare retention options

A paperboard pocket conceals the tool and can protect a neighbouring jar, but its opening must allow access. A strap makes the object visible but requires an attachment that cannot pull through the tray in normal handling. A separate wrapped compartment adds a packing step and must have space for the wrapping. Compare all three with the same actual accessory and record the packing sequence before selecting one.
Plan replenishment and artwork

If the tool is sourced separately, a revision in its supplier, finish or protective sleeve can affect the fit. Name the approved reference and surface condition in the packing sheet. Keep the tool’s narrow compartment clear of artwork essential to the recipient if the object will cover it. A packing proof should show which side faces up and where any safety sleeve is placed.

title: Perfume Travel Spray in a Gift Set: Prevent Label Scuff During Removal
seoTitle: Travel Spray Label Scuff in Gift Boxes | MTT
summary: A slim spray may pass a simple fit check and still pick up marks when it is rotated out of a snug cavity. Show the printed or labelled zone, seam, cap and any fragile coating on a physical component..
intro: A slim spray may pass a simple fit check and still pick up marks when it is rotated out of a snug cavity. Show the printed or labelled zone, seam, cap and any fragile coating on a physical component. Confirm with the product owner which areas are suitable for contact, including the difference between an empty container and the finished labelled unit.
cta: Share your filled product dimensions, weight, quantity per design and destination. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 in product value per order; freight, samples and other fees are excluded.
sections: Mark the surface that cannot rub

A slim spray may pass a simple fit check and still pick up marks when it is rotated out of a snug cavity. Show the printed or labelled zone, seam, cap and any fragile coating on a physical component. Confirm with the product owner which areas are suitable for contact, including the difference between an empty container and the finished labelled unit.
Trace the removal path

Observe the customer gripping the body, lifting the part and returning it to the insert. Draw the contact path through the cavity edge, not merely its resting position. A notch that makes the bottle easy to reach can change how it moves in the pack; verify both retention and access with the actual product.
Isolate the source of a mark

When a mark appears, record its position and compare it with the cavity edge, lid underside, adjacent bottle and any protective wrap. Change one variable at a time: orientation, contact surface or support geometry. Avoid attributing every rub mark to board grade or proposing a coating without a compatible material review.
Illustrative revision

A supplier increases the label height after the original sample. Reinsert the finished labelled part into the approved package and check whether the newly printed area meets a fold or cavity edge. Photograph the exact contact point, identify both revision numbers and agree whether a new sample or additional handling review is required. Product and packaging changes can affect the validity of distribution testing: ISTA retesting guidance.
Make the request specific

Send physical labelled components, dimensions with caps, filled weights, photos of unacceptable contact zones, target quantity and destination. Ask MTT to compare viable support and access options, then approve a representative sample. MOQ is 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 in product value per order; freight, sample costs and other fees are separate.
Compare the support contact

A folded card cradle may touch at discrete folds, while a fitted recess may contact a longer portion of the bottle. More contact is not automatically better or worse: the label finish, pressure and removal path matter. Test comparable complete samples and obtain the product owner’s decision about acceptable marks before signing off. If a sleeve is used, include its thickness and removal sequence in the review.
Give the sample a traceable result

Record which bottle, label lot and packaging revision were checked, the number of handling cycles agreed by the parties, lighting and the surfaces inspected. Distinguish a cosmetic mark from a structural failure. If the acceptance limit is undecided, label the result as an observation rather than a pass. This record gives the next supplier something specific to reproduce instead of a generic request for a softer insert.

title: Gift Box Sample Approval: Use Witness Marks to Find the Fit Problem
seoTitle: Gift Box Sample Fit: Find Witness Marks | MTT
summary: A buyer says a gift box is too tight. Before changing dimensions, identify whether the issue occurs at lid entry, final closure, drawer travel or product removal. Record the sample number, fully assembled.
intro: A buyer says a gift box is too tight. Before changing dimensions, identify whether the issue occurs at lid entry, final closure, drawer travel or product removal. Record the sample number, fully assembled components, orientation and the exact point where resistance begins. An empty shell and a loaded set can behave differently.
cta: Share your filled product dimensions, weight, quantity per design and destination. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 in product value per order; freight, samples and other fees are excluded.
sections: Turn a vague fault into a location

A buyer says a gift box is too tight. Before changing dimensions, identify whether the issue occurs at lid entry, final closure, drawer travel or product removal. Record the sample number, fully assembled components, orientation and the exact point where resistance begins. An empty shell and a loaded set can behave differently.
Inspect contact surfaces and sequence

Look for fresh rub, compression or crease marks on the sleeve interior, insert edges, bottle decoration and closure surfaces. Compare both sides of the contact pair. If tissue, a card or a pouch is part of the set, place it in the approved sequence; the additional layer may control clearance even though each individual component fits separately.
Change one part at a time

Suppose a loaded drawer catches near the end. Confirm the sleeve opening, tray outside, insert height and load distribution independently before changing more than one. Trial one proposed change, mark the new revision and repeat opening and product removal. Keep the previous sample as a comparison where practical; photographs alone may not show the source of resistance.
Separate a sample check from transport testing

A passing fit observation documents only the agreed sample and handling condition. The shipping carton, closure, orientation and route may create different stresses. Select and document an appropriate evaluation with the parties responsible for the product and distribution; ISTA recommends matching test selection to the actual distribution environment: ISTA test selection guidance.
Build an actionable approval record

List component versions, dimensions and filled weights, acceptable surfaces, artwork, observations, photos and the decision owner. State what changed since the last sample and who will approve the new version. Send MTT the reference, intended distribution and quantity for a custom quote. Minimum order: 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, sample and other fees.
A three-column fault record

Record the symptom, the two surfaces involved and the next controlled check. For a lid that stops early, compare the lid underside with the tallest loaded item. For a tray that catches near full opening, compare the tray walls and sleeve edge along the entire travel. For a scratched label, inspect the cavity edge and product withdrawal path. These are diagnostic starting points, not proof of a single cause.
When a revision changes the conclusion

A different paper wrap, added lamination, new glass supplier or modified card can change contact even when a nominal outside dimension stays the same. Mark the old and new versions on the brief and ask which previous sample decisions remain valid. If the change could affect transport performance, agree with the test owner whether to repeat relevant checks rather than treating an earlier result as transferable.
